what: Behind the page a WebGL contour terrain is laid — five layers of value-noise height drawn as thin lines (.34) at 18-cell spacing and thick lines (.62) every 5 cells, flowing slowly (only for the first 4 seconds and for 1.5 seconds after the cursor moves, stopping over 1 second). A wide hill under the cursor (gaussian exp(−5r²), strength .55) rises so the lines spread apart, and only the hill is tinted with the accent color — it follows the cursor position at .08 and the rise at .04 per step. Faint on the left (title side) and the bottom 30%. It does not redraw when idle

options.lines: Thin lines per 1 of height, default 18
options.follow: Rate of following the cursor position (per frame), default .08
options.rise: Ratio that follows the hill’s rise, default .04
options.fade: If none, the left side is not faded (version without a centered title)

use: <section data-fx="contour-terrain-gl">…Title · text…</section> — The canvas is laid at the very front of the panel with z-index −1. Colors are --kf-ink and --kf-accent (they follow when the theme changes)
note: Without WebGL2 nothing is laid down. Shaders are precompiled on attach (so the first cursor move doesn’t stall). On phones and reduce, the caller removes data-fx, and on devices without hover the hill doesn’t rise

from.where: index.html hero (.hero) — original hero-gl: fbm 1.35x · flow .018/.011 · lines 18 · thick lines /5 · hill exp(−5d²)×.55 · cursor .08 · rise .04 · first 4s · 1.5s after movement, only at (pointer: fine) and (min-width: 900px)
